variant_desc: malloc()/free() of 120B struct per iter, populated by cross-TU noinline init, hot field reads -> stack alloc + same init, no malloc per iter (variant 4: seed=46, n_scale=0.7x)
source_citation: Abseil Performance Tip #83 (2024-06-17): 'stats_info was only 120 bytes, so accessing its fields from data.stats_info might entail 4 cachelines.'
novelty_rationale: Tests recognition that small, locally-scoped structs should be stack-allocated rather than malloc'd. Compilers have heap-elision passes (LLVM, GCC) but they FAIL across TU boundaries, with custom allocators (tcmalloc/jemalloc), and when the pointer escapes via a noinline init function -- which is the typical real-world case. The fast version eliminates per-call malloc/free pairs and improves cache locality of field reads.
